title: Security ask interpretation, labeling, and fallback policy suggester
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create an interpreted metadata layer and automated suggestion engine for incoming enterprise security/compliance asks (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR/DPA/vendor questionnaires). The feature should: 1) parse customer submissions and vendor questionnaires to produce canonical labels (e.g., data residency, encryption, auditability, logging, human review), 2) surface a confidence score and suggested SLA tier, 3) propose a fallback plan (compatible model variant, regional hosting, dedicated capacity recommendation) and a recommended evidence bundle for a rapid response. The intention is to reduce manual triage time for the security & compliance team while giving account teams consistent, auditable recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming questionnaire or free-text ask is processed and returns a canonical label set with at least 6 common tags (data residency, PII, encryption, audit/logging, third-party access, SLAs)
System produces a confidence score (0-100) and recommended SLA tier (fast/standard/needs-enterprise-review) for 90% of test inputs
Suggested fallback policy contains at least one technical option (model variant or region) and one contractual option (DPA clause, limited data processing) for >80% of questions flagged high-risk
Dashboard exposes per-account histograms of ask categories, average triage time reduced by at least 30% in pilot accounts
Outputs are logged and linkable to evidence bundles and the support ticket; all outputs include an explanation string for auditors
Privacy: no raw customer data is persisted beyond allowed retention; KMS-protected artifact links are generated for evidence bundles
comments: 2026-02-24 - Kickoff: scoped MVP to support SOC2, GDPR, DPA checkbox-style and free-text fields. PM sync with Eng and Design. Action: engineering to prototype NL parsing approach.

2026-03-02 - Eng demo: prototype classifier (open-source transformer) achieves 0.78 F1 on internal labeled set. Trade-off: more labels improves recall but increases curator overhead. Agreed to start with 8 high-value tags.
2026-03-05 - Design review: added requirement for human-review path with editable suggested labels before sending to customer. UX will show suggested fallback policies with rationale.
2026-03-10 - Legal flagged GDPR data residency language; added a dependency for legal review on suggested contractual fallback templates (see dependency PM-27105).

2026-03-12 - Security review initiated: threat model completed. Key decision: inference of sensitive labels must run only inside Private deployment for enterprise accounts flagged as Tier-A. See decision notes below.
2026-03-15 - PM note: prepared pilot plan with three pilot customers; Eng to deliver API stub and dashboard tiles by 2026-03-28. Follow-up: schedule playbook walkthrough with Solutions team.
decisions: Use a hybrid approach: deterministic rules + light-weight transformer classifier to combine structured checkbox extraction with free-text interpretation
Start with a canonical tag set of 8 labels to reduce ambiguity; extend via taxonomy management in future releases
Expose suggested fallback policies as recommendations only; human operator must approve before sending to customers
Run sensitive inference inside Private deployments or Dedicated for Tier-A customers to meet compliance and data residency constraints
